course_description:
Entrepreneurship is commonly regarded as the pursuit of opportunity beyond the resources apparently to hand. With this maxim in mind, we explore the theory and practice of starting then growing new ventures, where opportunities exist but the pathways to unleash promising outcomes are uncertain. Knowledge and skill development is built by identifying and developing a new business idea within the class, through adaptive execution to generate information by building and testing business hypotheses so to navigate uncertainties. These skills are then used to analyse conditions across various entrepreneurial firms. Topics include the process of entrepreneurial logic, designing business models for value capture and delivery, framing competitive strategy, determining assumptions-based finance needs, understanding different innovation types and managing growth to build stronger ventures.

The primary purpose of this course is to excite students seeking an entrepreneurial, discovery-driven pathway for their careers — to challenge themselves to experience new ventures with uncertain outcomes, to determine how to form their own new venture, to manage innovation within an existing organisation, or to simply understand more about the entrepreneurial mindset. We will gain first-hand experience of leveraging opportunities and expanding our own personal entrepreneurial attributes through authentic, experiential learning.

This course is challenging, developing our awareness and practice across three streams. One stream involves team work to cultivate prospective new ventures, some of which may go on to evolve within the unique UQ ventures eco-system. Another stream allows frameworks shared in class to be applied to live case settings, developing analytical entrepreneurial skill. The third stream tests your theory application & analysis with a live case in the final exam.

Course Changes in Response to Previous Student Feedback

For Semester 2, 2026 the course actively builds your capability to use generative AI as an entrepreneurial tool — to interrogate assumptions, stress-test value propositions, accelerate evidence gathering and rehearse stakeholder perspectives across the venture you develop. A new seminar introduces effectuation as the decision lens that disciplines this AI work, so that AI outputs are treated as cheap experiments to test rather than predictions to follow. The A1 and A2 marking rubrics now also weave the Respectful Leaders graduate attribute alongside the existing Influential Communicators (A1) and Accomplished Scholars (A2) criteria — recognising inclusive team contribution in the pitch and video, and constructive peer engagement across the case-topic moderations.

The evaluation arc, streamlined for 2026, continues into Semester 2: the A1 presentations comprise a pitch and a video, each earning up to 20 marks (40 marks for the A1 stream). The A2 case topics stream remains a safe space to test principles covered in class, share your insights among your peers and moderate the insights of others in a circular learning environment, earning up to 20 marks. The final A3 case study (40 marks) is delivered as an invigilated, 2 hour exam drawing on case materials and reflective analysis shared prior to the central examination period.

Sustainable Development Goals - UQ Business School is a proud supporter and Advanced Signatory of the United Nations Principles for Responsible Management Education (UN PRME) . As part of the largest global collaboration between business schools and the UN, the school emphasises its role in empowering students to drive societal transformation through the Sustainable Development Goals . The SDGs highlight that a thriving economy relies on a healthy environment, aiming to balance economic growth, social well-being, and environmental protection for a sustainable future.

course_aims: This course aims to provide students with an understanding of the foundational principles of entrepreneurship and the contexts in which these principles can be applied. Students are exposed to the latest thinking on startups and creating new ventures. On conclusion of the course students should have a greater awareness of what it takes to launch a new venture and their suitability for this endeavour.

learning_outcomes.description: Articulate the foundational knowledge in the area of entrepreneurship.
Develop, evaluate and communicate actionable business opportunities as part of a startup team.
Create viable and innovative Business Models.
Critically analyse knowledge creation in the startup process.
Practice real-time entrepreneurial leadership to craft ideas and test impacts.

learning_activities.topic: S1 | New Ventures Introduce entrepreneurship, a history of entrepreneurial thought and its place in today's economy. Opportunity discovery & creation. Projects to develop. Assessment timelines. Student team formation. - Difference between small firms, entrepreneurial ventures and larger corporations - Entrepreneurial teams Learning outcomes: L01

S2 | Lean business models Using lean startup methods to shape business models and expose underlying growth drivers of value. Building a business model canvas informed using lean methods Learning outcomes: L01, L04
S3 | Discovery-driven Planning Developing assumptions to bring new products & services to market. Crafting an idea canvas. Exploring a DDP case. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03
S4 | Present venture pitch Deliver class presentation in your teams, showing how business model enables growth Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04, L05

S5 | Entrepreneurial AI Generative AI tools positioned as a new category of means within an effectual decision logic. We use AI to devise and evaluate new venture pathways through affordable-loss experiments and stakeholder rehearsals, building the critical judgement to recognise where AI overstates what it can actually deliver. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L04, L05

S6 | Entrepreneurial Strategy Entrepreneurial strategy frameworks: forming opportunity to gain competitive advantage & growth. Framing observed alignments to the four value-creation dynamics across customer-technology-capabilities-competition elements. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L04
S7 | Business Building Applying a discovery-driven growth orientation to scale with technology and business models. In-session work focuses on the team venture's build plan.

S8 | Entrepreneurial Leadership Drivers for design-led growth strategies and how to organise for emergent leadership paths in entrepreneurial ventures. Two organisational philosophies contrasted. In-class strategic simulation provides lived experience of leadership choices under uncertainty, with facilitator-scaffolded debrief on the choices observed and their consequences across the simulated market. Learning outcomes: L04, L05

S9 | Entrepreneurial Analyses Tools to interpret key attributes of proposed or existing firms, to leverage underlying value and to frame strategic capability-growth actions. Learning outcomes: L01, L03, L04

S10 | Disruptive innovation How technological & business model innovations can exploit asymmetric forces, for startups to displace resource-rich incumbents, or yield incremental improvements in product or service deliveries. Examine how innovations disrupt incumbents by crafting new market dynamics for 'good enough' products & services that substitute or complement current offerings Learning outcomes: L01, L02

S11 | Entrepreneurial Hypergrowth Exploring hypergrowth using chasm theory as a mechanism to predict technological dispersion and to pre-empt destructive growth forces. Stages traced from bowling alley through tornado to main street, with attention to the predictable pathologies that derail ventures at each transition. In-class growth simulation surfaces those pathologies as lived decisions, with facilitator-scaffolded debrief on the mistakes encountered. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L04, L05

S12 | Entrepreneurial Finance Exploring NPV and reverse financials as tools to interpret growth assumptions and accommodate uncertainty in finance models. Apply finance models to prospective ventures to interpret capital needs and long-term value potential including returns to founders and investors. An in-class ownership-allocation role play closes the session as a final integrative experience — translating finance theory into the lived decision of how value is shared among those who built it. Learning outcomes: L01, L04

S13 | Navigating Uncertainty Reflecting on the journey through the course in preparation for the A3 final exam. The session workshops the live-case research approach and A4 note craft you will use under invigilated conditions. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04, L05
